lawyer:
Dr Kamal Hossain with M Amir-ul-Islam, Advocates ------ For the Petitioner. 
Md Helaluddin Mollah, Deputy Attorney-General with Md Alamgir Kabir Assistant Attorney-General ------ For the State.
parties:
Dr Qazi Faruque Ahmed ------ Accused-Petitioner
Vs.
State represented by the Deputy Commissioner ------ Opposite Party
full_judgment:
Nozrul Islam Chowdhury J: This Rule under section 498 of the Code of Criminal Procedure was issued at the instance of the petitioner asking the opposite party to show cause why the petitioner Dr Qazi Faruque Ahmed should not be enlarged on bail in Pallabi PS Case No. 31(6) 2004 dated 20-6-2004 now pending before the Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Dhaka and or such other or further order or orders passed as to this Court may seem fit and proper. 

 2. Facts relevant for the purpose of disposal of this Rule is that on 20-6-04 at 15.30 hours a first information report was lodged with Pallabi Police Station by one Md Abdur Rahim Khan, Sub-Inspector of Police under Pallabi Police Station, Dhaka Metropolitan Police alleging, inter alia. that on 7-3-2004 in the evening a meeting took place at Proshika Bhaban where 7 accused persons including the petitioner were present and in the said meeting the petitioner disclosed that the government of the ruling. alliance has to be overthrown and party in opposition should be supported to take over power whereby they will have some privilege for operating their organisation namely, Proshika. It is alleged further in the said first information report that the petitioner also asked his companions to go for arranging a movement to overthrow the government and also disclosed some ways and means for the purpose. It is alleged further in the first information report that the petitioner also asked for arranging a mass rally in Dhaka for the aforesaid purposes. With the allegation as aforesaid, the instant case was brought with the police station, which was registered under section 120A and 120B/34 of the Penal Code. 

 3. Prior, the lodging of the first information report in connection with this case the petitioner was apprehended by the police in a different case and subsequently, he was shown arrested in the present case. 

 4. Thereafter, the petitioner filed an application for bail before the Metropolitan Sessions Judge, Dhaka in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 1688 of 2004 which, after hearing, was rejected by the learned Metropolitan Sessions Judge by his order dated 24-6-2004. 

 6. Dr Kamal Hossain, learned Counsel, appearing with Mr Amir-ul Islam for the petitioner, submits at the outset that the petitioner is an aged man of 57 years and a law abiding, peace loving and respectable citizen of Bangladesh. He is also a freedom fighter and has been dedicated to bring social and economic change and development in Bangladesh by eradicating poverty through creation of a democratic society thereby achieving the goal of social uplift, It is also submitted by Dr Hossain that the petitioner is the president of Proshika, one of the leading NGOs in Bangladesh with 1.14 crore beneficiaries and number of its staff consists of 9000 persons and he is widely respected nationally and internationally for his contribution to economic development in Bangladesh and has been awarded an honorary 'Doctor of Laws' degree from Bath University in the United Kingdom. Dr Hossain also submitted that the petitioner is in ill-health and has been suffering for some years from a schaemic heart disease, and diabetic retinopathy and requires regular monitoring of his blood pressure, blood sugar levels and daily insulin injections as well. The learned Counsel for the petitioner submits further that there is no chance of abscondence or of tampering with the evidence on the part of the petitioner, in the event of his being enlarged on bail. Dr Hossain submits lastly that the allegations as brought against the petitioner in the first information report do not attract the ingredients of the offence under section 124A and 120B of the Penal Code. Therefore, it is submitted that there are reasonable grounds for believing that the petitioner is not guilty of the offence alleged. Finally, Dr Hossain pointed out that a respectable aged man like the petitioner has been languishing in custody for about 3 months who has been implicated in series of case, one after anothers, including the present one, as such, from the facts and circumstances, it appears that the detention of the petitioner in custody is an outcome of malicious attitude towards him by the authority concerned. 

 7. Mr Helaluddin Mollah, learned Deputy Attorney-General appearing with Mr Alamgir Kabir, learned Assistant Attorney-General on behalf of the State, opposes the Rule with the submission that here is a case which has been initiated only on 20-6-2004 and the investigation is yet to be over and in course of investigation if the petitioner is enlarged on bail then, in that case there is every possibility on his part to interfere with the process of investigation as also tampering with the evidence thereof. The Deputy Attorney-General also pointed out that co-accused Abdur Rob made a confession on 24-5-2004 before the Magistrate, 1st Class, Manikganj disclosing the complicity of the petitioner in this case in specific terms. Therefore, this petitioner does not deserve bail in the present case at this stage, which involves capital punishment as well. 

 8. Heard the learned Councels, perused the petition and the relevant materials on record. It is to be noted at the outset that despite service of notice upon the opposite party, in due course, no counter affidavit on its behalf, has been filed to controvert the assertions made on oath by the petitioner in his application under section 498 of the Code of Criminal Procedure. Under such circumstances we find in paragraph 5 thereof the petitioner has stated on oath that he has been implicated in several cases of which he disclosed 8 cases which were brought on the same day i.e 16-5-04. In paragraph 7 of the said application we also find two other cases in which the petitioner has been implicated. It is also evident from paragraph 8 that the petitioner was ordered to be taken on remand, which however was averted by the petitioner with an interference of this Court. From paragraph 14 of the said application we find that specific averments made on oath, to the effect that the petitioner has been falsely implicated in the case with ulterior motive and in order to harass the petitioner and destroy his prestige and reputation in the eyes of the public, though the petitioner is innocent. Those averments made on oath remain unassailed as indicated above, as such, we have no reason to discard those at this stage. 

 9. From the order passed by the Metropolitan Sessions Judge Dhaka refusing prayer for bail by the petitioner, it appears that the learned Metropolitan Sessions Judge has refused the same simply on the ground that the investigation of the case was going on. We have also noticed that since the date of passing of the order by the learned Metropolitan Sessions Judge on 24-6-04 a period of about a month more has elapsed, yet the police could not submit its report after investigation in the case. This is, however, a matter to be dealt with by the investigating agency but the fact remains that no police report has been submitted in this case so far. We have also noticed that in the application  the petitioner has made a statement on oath to the effect that he is an ailing man and requires medical care, which is not possible inside the jail. 

 10. Under the circumstances stated above, we find that the apprehension of the learned Deputy Attorney-General to the effect that there is possibility on the part of the petitioner to interfere with the process of investigation and of tampering with the evidence, has got no basis at all. From the attending facts and circumstances of the case, we feel inclined to enlarge the petitioner of bail with certain conditions. 

 11. In the result, this Rule is made absolute and the petitioner Dr Qazi Faruque Ahmed is hereby enlarged on bail to the satisfaction of Deputy Commissioner, Dhaka in Pallabi PS Case No. 31 (6) 2004 dated 20-6-2004 till framing of the charge, if any, in this case and in the event of framing of charge against the petitioner the trial Court shall have the liberty to deal with the question of bail of the accused-petitioner in accordance with law.
